home.desc.value: Zirve is a free logic puzzle game for iPhone and iPad: climb a tower where every floor is a short puzzle from {puzzleTypes} types. Daily tower, weekly league. No forced ads.

home.hero_alt.value: Zirve home screen: the forest tower at floor 16

daily.title.value: Daily tower: the same {dailyFloors} floors for everyone · Zirve

home.chip.value: For iPhone and iPad · on the App Store

home.h1_html.value: Climb the tower. Every floor a puzzle.

home.lead.value: Zirve is an endless tower of quick puzzles. Solve one, climb a floor, reach the next camp and pass your friends in the weekly league.

home.how_h2.value: Under a minute. Understood in five seconds.

home.how_p.value: Every floor is a single puzzle. You get the rules at a glance; as you climb the board gets harder, not the clock.

home.games_p.value: Each floor brings a different game; every 10 floors there is a camp and a new game. The first time you meet one, a short animation shows how it works before the clock starts, and the ? button brings it back during play. Every board is solved by the computer before you see it: no unsolvable puzzles.

home.worlds_p.value: A new world every 20 floors: from the forest to flower slopes, from storms to northern lights, from galaxies to the Endless Summit. The higher you climb, the harder the puzzles and the brighter the worlds.

footer.tag.value: Climb the tower, every floor a puzzle.

home.cta_p.value: Zirve is free on the App Store. The first floors are waiting.

value: Tap Climb and meet the floor's puzzle: colours, paths, blocks or cards.
You have 30–60 seconds. Miss it by a hair and the board waits for you; take a breath and finish.
A camp every 10 floors gives a life back and unlocks a new game. Even when your lives run out, your record stays.

value.goal: Bring matching tiles together and clear the board.
how: Drag a tile onto a neighbour of the same colour: both disappear.
Drag into an empty square to slide a tile closer to its pair.
harder: From floor 10: walls and tiles with a limited number of slides (frozen at 0)
From floor 30: every tile has a slide limit, up to 6 colours
From floor 60: locked tiles that open when a match happens next to them

value.goal: Reach the flag with one line, without lifting your finger.
how: Draw from node to node; pull back to undo the last step.
Pass the checkpoints and end on the flag. Lift your finger and the line resets.
harder: From floor 20: fog, you only see around your pen
From floor 30: checkpoints in order
From floor 60: visit every node, more walls

value.goal: Fit every piece into the gaps on the board.
how: Drag a piece from the tray onto the board; tap a piece to turn it.
Tap a placed piece to take it back; the floor is done when everything fits.
harder: From a 6×6 board to 8×8, from 3 pieces to 6
From floor 30: mirrored pieces you flip with a long press
Bigger pieces, tighter gaps

value.goal: Flip the cards and find the matches.
how: Turn two cards: a match stays open, otherwise they close again shortly.
Remember where each card is and find every pair.
harder: From 12 cards to 24
From floor 30: triples, find three of the same picture
Wrong cards close faster

value.goal: Connect matching ends and fill the board.
how: Draw a line from a coloured dot to its matching dot.
Lines can't cross and every square must be filled; an unfinished line vanishes when you lift your finger.
harder: From a 5×5 board to 7×7
From 3 colours to 6
Blocked squares you have to route around

value.goal: Turn the pipes and get the water flowing.
how: Tap a pipe to turn it 90 degrees.
Lead the water from the source to the flag without a gap; flowing pipes fill up.
harder: From floor 40: every pipe must be connected
More branches, more tangled pipes
A 6×6 board from floor 100

value.goal: Sort the colours until every tube holds one.
how: Tap a tube, then another: the top colour pours over.
It only goes onto the same colour or into an empty tube; stuck? Undo.
harder: From 4 colours to 8
More mixed starts, longer solutions
Always two empty tubes: the planning is yours

value.goal: Clear the arrows in the right order.
how: Tap an arrow: it slides the way its head points, its body follows, and it leaves the board if the way is clear.
If another arrow is in the way, it bumps back and costs 3 seconds; clear the ones in front first.
harder: From a 7×7 board to 11×11, up to 85% full
Short arrows next to winding snakes up to 12 cells long
Longer "this one first" chains

value.goal: Lead every block out through the gate of its own colour.
how: Drag a block: it only slides the way its arrows point. With a clear way it leaves through the matching gate; a tap is enough.
The first move is never an exit: you have to park a block aside to open a way first.
harder: From a 6×6 board to 8×8, from 7 blocks to 14
At least 3, later 4 planned parks on every board
From floor 80 a locked block; from floor 100 a 2×2 block that slides any direction

value.goal: Place one lookout tower in every row, column and coloured region.
how: Tap a square: first ✕ (a note), tap again for a lookout. Every row, column and region needs exactly one.
Lookouts never touch, not even diagonally. Every board has exactly one solution; no guessing, just logic.
harder: From a 6×6 board to 8×8
On the first boards ruled-out squares are dotted for you; later you mark them yourself
Longer chains of deduction

how: Tap a square: it and its up, down, left and right neighbours (a + shape) flip. Dark ones light up, lit ones go dark.
Hold your finger down to see which squares will flip; diagonals are not affected.
harder: From a 3×3 board to 5×5
From 3 to 10 taps to solve
Order matters: think first, then tap

home.worlds_h2.value: {worlds} worlds, a tower without an end.

home.league_p.value: Every week you join a league of {leagueSize} players. The floors you clear this week set your rank; the top {leaguePromote} move up a tier, the bottom {leagueRelegate} move down. Everyone shows with their chosen name, outfit and tower theme; pull down to refresh the standings instantly.

value: The same {dailyFloors} floors for everyone, {dailyAttempts} attempts. Gems at floors 3, 6 and 10; where do you rank in your country and among friends?
A new reward track every month: earn gems, outfits and tower themes as you climb. Each season brings its own exclusive outfit and theme.
Share your invite code, see where everyone is in the tower, get a heads-up when you pass them.
A chest every 10 clean floors (5–20 gems), a star chest every 20 stars. One floor a day keeps your streak alive.

value.p: Boards are solved as they are generated; it comes down to your moves, not luck.
Start right away. Sign in with Apple if you like, and your progress follows you to a new device.
Keep climbing on the train or a plane; your floors sync when you are back online.
Every tile has a shape as well as a colour; playable with VoiceOver; Time assist gives more or unlimited time.
Ads appear only when you ask for one: for a life or extra time. No interruptions.

value: Yes. Downloading and playing are free. Gem packs, the starter pack, the season set and the season's premium reward track are optional in-app purchases, billed by Apple.
iPhone and iPad on iOS 18 or later, iPhone 11 and newer. There is no Android version for now.
No. A guest account is created for you on first launch. To move your progress to another device, sign in with Apple.
What if the time is too short for me?
Turn on Settings → Time assist for 1.5× or unlimited time on every floor. Stars still use the normal time and assisted floors don't count for the weekly league.
What happens when I run out of lives?
You have three lives. When they are gone you return to camp, but your record stays. Lives refill over time and reaching a camp gives one back; you can also refill by watching an ad or with gems.
We only process what the game needs to work; see the Privacy Policy. The rules of the game are in the Terms of Use.
How do I delete my account?
In the app: Profile → Settings → Account → Delete account. See Delete your account.

daily.desc.value: The same {dailyFloors} floors for everyone, {dailyAttempts} attempts. Climb today's tower in Zirve and share your result.

daily.lead.value: Every day, the same ten floors for everyone and three attempts. Your best attempt is ranked. When you share your result, the games and boards stay hidden, so nobody's surprise is spoiled.

daily.card_label.value: Sample result: 7 of 10 floors in 3 minutes 5 seconds

daily.grid_p.value: Each square of a shared result is one floor: top row 1–5, bottom row 6–10. Every square has its own colour and icon, so it reads without colour too.

daily.assist.value: A 🕒 With time assist line means Time assist was on during the attempt. The squares still follow the normal time; assisted attempts are not ranked.

daily.note.value: Got Zirve? Tap Open in the banner at the top of this page to go straight to the daily tower.

daily.cta_p.value: Zirve is free on the App Store. Today's tower is waiting.

value: Solved with at least 15 seconds left.
Solved before the time ran out.
Time ran out; solved after continuing with an ad or gems.
The attempt ended on this floor.
The attempt did not get this far.
In Zirve, tap the Daily tower card on the tower screen. It renews every midnight and is the same for everyone.
Every floor is a quick puzzle. You get three attempts; the best one is ranked in your country and among friends. Gems at floors 3, 6 and 10.
When the attempt is over, tap Share result: the squares and your time go out, the games and boards don't.

games.desc.value: All {puzzleTypes} puzzle types in Zirve, the free logic puzzle tower for iPhone and iPad: what each one asks of you, when it opens and how it gets harder.

games.lead.value: Every floor of the tower is one of these games. Four are open from the first floor, and a new one joins at each camp after that. Each page below has the rules, how the puzzle grows as you climb, tips and a real screenshot.

games.aka_h2.value: What this kind of puzzle is called

value.desc: Color match in Zirve: drag a tile onto a neighbour of the same colour and both disappear. Rules, slide limits, locked tiles and tips.
value.intro: Color match is the first game of the tower: drag a tile onto a neighbour of the same colour and both leave the board. Tiles slide square by square, and higher up each tile can only slide a limited number of times.
tips: From floor 10, the number in a tile's corner is how many squares it can still slide. Spend slides on the tile that is far from its pair.
A tile at 0 can no longer slide, but it can still merge: bring its partner to it instead.
Walls cannot be entered. Find the route around them before you start dragging.
From floor 60, a locked tile opens when any match happens right next to it. Plan that match early.
If the slides left are not enough to finish, tap Restart to bring the board back to its start. The clock keeps running, so do it early.
value.aka: It belongs to the family of tile-matching puzzles, where two equal pieces meet and disappear. In Zirve tiles slide square by square, and from floor 10 every slide is counted. Each colour also has its own shape, so the board can be read without colour.

value.desc: Path draw in Zirve: draw one line from node to node and reach the flag without lifting your finger. Rules, fog, ordered checkpoints and tips.
value.intro: Path draw asks for a single line: move from node to node without lifting your finger, pass the checkpoints and end on the flag. Higher up the board fills with walls and fog, and finally the line must visit every node.
tips: Keep your finger down. If you lift it before the board is solved, the line resets to the start.
Pull back along your line to undo the last steps; it is faster than starting over.
Do not split the board in two: if your line cuts the free nodes into separate areas, you cannot visit both.
On boards where every node must be visited, a node with only two free neighbours has to be entered from one and left by the other. Fix those forced steps in your head first.
From floor 30 the checkpoints are numbered and you cannot enter one before its turn, so plan a route that meets them in order.
value.aka: This is a one-line or one-stroke drawing puzzle. Classic one-stroke puzzles ask you to trace every edge of a figure; in Zirve you visit nodes instead, so the old rule about an odd number of connections does not apply here.

value.desc: Block fit in Zirve: drag and rotate pieces until they fill the gaps on the board exactly. Rules, mirror pieces from floor 30 and tips.
value.intro: Block fit is a packing puzzle: drag the pieces from the tray onto the board until every gap is filled. Tap to rotate; higher up, some pieces only fit after you flip them.
tips: Start with the largest or oddest piece. Small pieces can fill whatever is left.
Fill corners and narrow gaps first: few pieces fit there.
Count squares. If a gap has a size no remaining piece can make, something is in the wrong place: tap a placed piece to send it back to the tray.
From floor 30, a piece with the ↻ badge will not fit by rotating alone. Press and hold it to flip it.
When the line under the board turns red and says undo, a piece already placed is blocking the rest.
value.aka: Packing puzzles with pieces made of squares are known as polyomino or pentomino puzzles, and tangram works the same way with triangles. In Zirve the empty space is cut from the pieces themselves, so every board has an exact fit.

value.desc: Memory in Zirve: flip two cards at a time and find every pair. Board sizes, triples from floor 30 and tips for remembering positions.
value.intro: Memory is the classic card game: flip two cards, keep them open if they match and try again if they do not. As you climb the board grows, wrong cards close faster and from floor 30 you look for triples.
tips: The first time round, flip cards in a fixed order, row by row. Positions are easier to recall that way.
When a card matches one you have already seen, go for the pair right away.
Wrong cards close faster as you climb. Say the picture and its place to yourself as you flip.
In triples, two open cards that differ end the attempt at once, so open the card you are sure of second.
value.aka: It is also known as concentration, pairs or matching cards. Zirve adds a version with three equal cards from floor 30.

value.desc: Flow in Zirve: join every pair of matching ends with lines that never cross, and fill the whole board. Rules, board sizes and tips.
value.intro: Flow asks you to join each pair of matching ends with a line. Lines cannot cross, every square can hold only one line, and the board is only solved when every square is filled.
tips: Start with pairs along the edges and in the corners: their lines have the fewest ways to go.
Every square must be filled, so a line that leaves a one-square pocket is wrong. Let lines hug the walls and each other.
An empty corner square has only two neighbours, so a line must pass through it along the edge.
Draw a line in one go. Lifting your finger before you reach its pair erases it; finished lines stay.
Going back over your own line shortens it, and starting again from an end resets that colour.
value.aka: These puzzles are often called connect the dots or line puzzles. Some versions only ask you to join the pairs; Zirve's version always asks you to fill the whole board too.

value.desc: Pipe turn in Zirve: rotate the pipe pieces until water flows from the source to the flag, later through every piece. Rules and tips.
value.intro: Pipe turn fills the board with pipe pieces: ends, straights, corners and T pieces. Tap a piece to turn it a quarter turn and make the water run from the source to the flag; from floor 40, every piece must join the flow.
tips: Start next to the source and the flag. They never turn, so the pieces beside them have fewer possible directions.
Pieces on the edge of the board cannot point outwards. Turn them inwards first.
Each tap is a quarter turn clockwise. A straight piece needs at most one tap, any other piece at most three.
From floor 40 every piece must join the network: an open end pointing at the wall or at a piece that does not answer means something is still wrong.
The count above the board shows how many squares the water reaches. Use it to check your progress.
value.aka: This type is known as a pipe puzzle, a plumber puzzle or a network puzzle. In Zirve the source and the flag stay fixed and the board never starts solved.

value.desc: Color sort in Zirve: pour coloured stones between tubes until each tube holds one colour. Pouring rules, undo and tips.
value.intro: Color sort gives you tubes of mixed coloured stones and two empty tubes. Tap a tube to lift its top stones of one colour and tap another to pour them; the tube is solved when it holds four stones of a single colour.
tips: You can only pour onto the same colour or into an empty tube. Keep one tube empty for as long as you can: it is your free space.
Before using an empty tube, look for a tube whose top already matches.
Finish one colour at a time. A full tube of one colour no longer gets in the way.
If no move helps, tap Undo instead of filling your last empty tube.
Every colour also has its own shape, so you can sort by shape if colours are hard to tell apart.
value.aka: This is the water sort or ball sort type of puzzle. In Zirve the tubes hold coloured stones rather than water, and there are always two empty tubes.

value.desc: Arrows in Zirve: tap an arrow and it slides off the board if its path is clear. Rules, bent arrows, the 3-second penalty and tips.
value.intro: Arrows fills the board with straight and bent arrows. Tap one and it slides off the board in the direction of its head, but only if the line from its head to the edge is empty; a blocked arrow bounces back and costs time.
tips: Look from the arrowhead to the edge of the board. If nothing is on that line, the arrow is free.
Removing an arrow never blocks another one, so take every free arrow you see.
Start near the edges, where exit lines are short.
A bent arrow leaves in the direction of its head, not its tail. Follow the body to the head before you tap.
A blocked tap costs 3 seconds on the clock. In calm mode there is no clock, so you can try freely.
value.aka: This kind of puzzle is called an arrow puzzle or an arrow escape puzzle. In Zirve a blocked arrow costs time rather than a life, and long arrows bend like snakes.

value.desc: Gates in Zirve: slide blocks along their lanes and lead each one out through the gate of its own colour. Rules, parking, locked blocks and tips.
value.intro: Gates is a sliding block puzzle: blocks move only along their long side, and each one leaves the board through a gate of its own colour. No block can leave on the first move, so the puzzle is deciding which block to park where.
tips: Find a block close to its gate and see what stands in its way. That is usually the block to move first.
Park the blocking piece where it does not close another block's lane.
A block leaving never blocks anything, so let every block out as soon as its way is clear.
Read the line under the board: when a move does not happen it tells you why, such as a locked block, the wrong gate or a closed path.
From floor 80 a grey block is locked. It opens only after every block of its key colour has left.
value.aka: Sliding block and parking puzzles are an old family; a well-known example is the Chinese Klotski puzzle. Zirve's version differs in that blocks leave through gates of their own colour instead of one shared exit.

value.desc: Lookouts in Zirve: place one lookout tower in every row, column and coloured region, with no two touching. Rules and solving tips.
value.intro: Lookouts is a logic placement puzzle: put one lookout tower in every row, every column and every coloured region, and no two towers may touch, not even diagonally. Every board has exactly one solution and can be solved without guessing.
tips: Tap once for a ✕ note and again for a lookout. Drag across empty squares to mark many ✕ at once.
Around every lookout, mark the eight touching squares with ✕.
If a region lies entirely in one row, no other region can use that row: mark the rest of the row with ✕. The same works for columns.
If two regions together fit inside exactly two rows, the other regions cannot use those two rows.
A small region decides quickly. Start there and let the crosses spread.
value.aka: This is a placement puzzle in the Star Battle family, with one piece per row, column and region. Zirve uses lookout towers as the pieces.

value.desc: Lights in Zirve: tap a square to flip it and its neighbours until the whole board is lit. Rules, board sizes and a step-by-step method.
value.intro: Lights is the last game to open and the most mathematical one: tapping a square flips it and its four neighbours, lit to dark and dark to lit. The floor is solved when every square is lit.
tips: The order of taps does not matter, and two taps on the same square cancel out. Every square needs at most one tap.
Work row by row: tap the square under each dark square of the row above. The dark squares move down until only the bottom row is left.
The pattern left in the bottom row tells you which squares of the top row to tap. Tap them and work down again.
A tap in a corner changes three squares, on an edge four, in the middle five. Corners are good for small fixes.
value.aka: It is a version of the puzzle known as lights out, named after a handheld game from the 1990s. In Zirve the goal is reversed: light every square.

press.short.value: Zirve is a free logic puzzle game for iPhone and iPad. You climb a tower where every floor is a short, timed puzzle from {puzzleTypes} types, from color sort and pipes to arrows and sliding blocks. There is a daily tower, weekly leagues and a calm mode with no timer, and no forced ads.

value: Zirve turns short logic puzzles into a climb. Every floor of the tower is one puzzle with a timer: solve it to go up, collect up to three stars and reach a camp every ten floors. Four games are open from the first floor and a new one joins at each camp, until all {puzzleTypes} are in the mix: color match, path draw, block fit, memory, flow, pipe turn, color sort, arrows, gates, lookouts and lights.

Every board is generated and solved by the computer before it is shown, so no puzzle is unsolvable. The daily tower gives everyone the same ten floors each day, with three attempts. Weekly leagues put players into groups of {leagueSize}, and monthly seasons add a reward path, outfits and tower themes.

Zirve is made by mm-apps, an independent developer in Türkiye, and is available in {appLanguageCount} languages. It shows no forced ads: an ad plays only when a player asks for a reward. Time assist with 1.5× or unlimited time, VoiceOver support and a shape for every colour make it playable for more people.
